statement: For t in closure(U) minus U, U/t is a point or the three-object category with terminal middle vertex, except at the four points t=(epsilon,eta) with epsilon in {1,2n-1}, eta in {1,2m-1}, where it is tilde(Psi).
repair: The downset of an interior even coordinate is a singleton; that of an odd coordinate is a three-object cospan. Intersect the product downset with the endpoint boundary to obtain the stated cases.
references: Commentary: The boundary and its categorical closure

statement: The five-object category tilde(Psi)=(a prime->a<-0->b<-b prime) is contractible but has no terminal object.
repair: Its underlying nerve is a path; a and b are incomparable maximal objects.

statement: U\hookrightarrow X is not an open Dwyer inclusion.
repair: At each exceptional corner t_i the slice U/t_i has no terminal object, so U\to closure(U) has no right adjoint.

statement: U\hookrightarrow X minus {t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4} is an open Dwyer inclusion.
repair: All slices over its generated cosieve now have terminal objects; in a poset these assemble uniquely into a right adjoint.

statement: U\hookrightarrow X is not a W_infinity-cofibration, meaning its cobase-change functor on undercategories fails to preserve weak equivalences.
gap_or_error: The proof on ms.15 uses a false fundamental-group calculation and invokes an inverse excision principle not valid for W_infinity in general.
repair: The six-object pushout has classifying space S^3. Closed Dwyer inclusions at the corner transfer it to the rectangle; the explicit witness q_U in W_infinity with q not in W_infinity completes the proof.
references: Commentary: The pushout is a three-sphere; Carrying the local obstruction to the boundary

statement: Let V be the corner subcategory {(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)} of U, isomorphic to Psi.
gap_or_error: The PDF first prints F\hookrightarrow U and then labels the corner [V=].
repair: The consistent symbol is V; retain the source F and editorial bracket in the transcription, recording an edition slip.

statement: V\hookrightarrow U is a closed Dwyer inclusion, whose smallest open neighbourhood is tilde(Psi)=U/t_1.
repair: The neighbourhood consists of V together with (2,0),(0,2); send those two extra objects to (1,0),(0,1). This is left adjoint to the inclusion.
references: Commentary: Carrying the local obstruction to the boundary

statement: V\hookrightarrow U is a W_infinity-cofibration.
repair: Apply the dual of Thomason's Dwyer pushout theorem; the property is preserved under cobase change.

statement: If U\to X were a W-cofibration, then V\to X would be a W-cofibration because V\to U is one.
repair: Cobase-change functors compose, so preservation of weak equivalences is closed under composition.

statement: The closure bar(V) of V in X is the square on (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1).
repair: These and only these are successors of the three corner points.

statement: bar(V)\hookrightarrow X is a closed Dwyer inclusion.
repair: Its smallest open neighbourhood is {0,1,2}^2. Coordinatewise 0->0, 1->1, 2->1 gives the left adjoint.
references: Commentary: Carrying the local obstruction to the boundary

statement: The smallest open neighbourhood W of bar(V) is the displayed nine-object product {0,1,2}^2.
notes: This W is a category, not the localizer W.

statement: For every s in this neighbourhood outside bar(V), the comma category s\backslash bar(V) has an initial object; for s=a prime,b prime it is [1], and for the other three choices it is a point.
repair: At (2,0), the reachable corner objects form (1,0)->(1,1); at (0,2) the dual coordinate gives the other chain; (2,1),(1,2),(2,2) only reach (1,1).

statement: bar(V)\to X is a W_infinity-cofibration.
repair: The dual Dwyer theorem applies.

statement: There is p:V\to V prime such that the pushout along V\hookrightarrow bar(V) has i,p in W_infinity but i prime,bar(p) outside W_infinity.
gap_or_error: The recalled example is correct, but the stated reason on ms.15 contains errors.
repair: Take V_0 prime=Z, V prime=Z^triangleright and compute the pushout Q as the double terminal cone on Z. Then BQ=S^3.
references: Commentary: The pushout is a three-sphere

statement: p_0:V\to V_0 prime=Z is the full inclusion of the original span as a closed subcategory.
gap_or_error: The source prints V prime and immediately corrects it to V_0 prime in editorial brackets.
repair: Retain the editorial correction; the underlying inclusion is the cosieve excluding the new source 0 prime.

statement: p_{0!}(e_V)=e_{V_0 prime}.
repair: Presheaf left Kan extension sends the canonical colimit of the three representables on V to the pointwise singleton pushout on Z.
references: Commentary: The missing retraction and the two-sphere

statement: V prime is obtained by adjoining a terminal object e to V_0 prime; the presentation adds rho:a->e, sigma:b->e with rho alpha=sigma beta.
repair: The given relations also identify the two paths from 0 prime to e, so every object has exactly one arrow to e.

statement: p_1:V_0 prime\hookrightarrow V prime is open, and p=p_1p_0:V\to V prime.
notes: A terminal-cone inclusion is a sieve because the new terminal object has no arrows to old objects.

statement: V,bar(V),V prime are W_infinity-aspherical, hence i and p are weak equivalences.
repair: V has an initial object; bar(V) and V prime have terminal objects.

statement: Q=bar(V prime) is not W_infinity-aspherical, equivalently i prime:V prime\to Q is not in W_infinity.
gap_or_error: The source argues via the inappropriate inverse excision criterion and the wrong pi_1 of the link.
repair: Compute BQ=S^3 directly. Since BV prime is contractible, i prime cannot be a weak equivalence.
references: Commentary: The pushout is a three-sphere

statement: Q minus V prime is the singleton category {t}, identified with bar(V) minus V.
repair: The pushout adds exactly the original square's missing terminal vertex; no objects of V prime are identified with it.

statement: Assuming W(7 bis), i prime belongs to W if and only if V prime/t is W-aspherical.
gap_or_error: The printed footnote explicitly invokes W(7 bis), whose inverse form is not valid for W_infinity without additional hypotheses. Singleton complement alone is insufficient.
repair: For this particular example the double-cone computation proves the conclusion. For the general converse, an acyclic non-simply-connected link gives a counterexample; see the later acyclic-link block.
references: Grothendieck1990XII, ms.149--150, Corollary 4 and note 104; commentary: The pushout is a three-sphere; Acyclic links and a false converse
notes: Recorded as an explicit conditional assumption, not as an unconditional modern theorem.

statement: V prime/t is isomorphic to V_0 prime.
repair: Exactly the objects of V_0 prime have a unique arrow to t; e has none. Morphisms in the slice are the unchanged arrows of V_0 prime.

statement: pi_1(V_0 prime) is isomorphic to Z.
gap_or_error: Contradicts the corrected two-sphere calculation on ms.11, footnote 7; the formula is present in the PDF.
repair: pi_1(V_0 prime)=0 and pi_2(V_0 prime)=Z.
references: Grothendieck1990XIIapp, ms.11, footnote 7; commentary: The missing retraction and the two-sphere

statement: V_0 prime is non-W-aspherical whenever W is contained in W_1, by its alleged nontrivial fundamental group.
gap_or_error: Taking W=W_1 refutes this: V_0 prime has trivial fundamental group and is connected.
repair: Its S^2 type detects nonasphericity for W_infinity (and W contained in W_2). The pushout Q has S^3 type and therefore the failure of i prime is detected for W contained in W_3, not W_1 or W_2.
references: Commentary: The pushout is a three-sphere
notes: For more general localizers one must also retain the pushout-stability hypotheses; the standing section convention is W=W_infinity.

statement: In the pasted diagram V->bar(V)->X over V prime->Q->X prime, the right square is a categorical pushout and is W_infinity-homotopy cocartesian.
repair: Associativity of pushouts gives the categorical square; bar(V)\to X is a closed Dwyer inclusion, so Thomason's theorem and opposites give the homotopy comparison.
references: Thomason1980, Proposition 4.3; commentary: Carrying the local obstruction to the boundary

statement: In this square, bar(p) belongs to W_infinity if and only if q belongs to W_infinity.
gap_or_error: A homotopy pushout alone does not reflect weak equivalences; the source leaves the additional reason implicit.
repair: bar(V)\to X is a weak equivalence between contractible spaces. Its Dwyer pushout Q\to X prime is also a weak equivalence. The displayed biconditional now follows by two-out-of-three.
references: Commentary: Carrying the local obstruction to the boundary
notes: The biconditional is true in this example; it is not recorded as a false general theorem.

statement: The resulting p is in W_infinity but q is not, proving V\to X is not a W_infinity-cofibration.
repair: Bp has contractible source and target; BX is contractible, while BX prime is weakly equivalent to BQ=S^3.
references: Commentary: Carrying the local obstruction to the boundary

statement: Factoring through U produces U prime=U\amalg_VV prime, and q_U:U\to U prime belongs to W_infinity.
repair: It is the pushout of the weak equivalence p along the closed Dwyer inclusion V\to U.

statement: The pushout of q_U along U\to X is the same map q:X\to X prime; hence U\to X fails to be a W_infinity-cofibration.
gap_or_error: Depends on the corrected proof that q is not a weak equivalence.
repair: Associativity identifies X\amalg_UU prime with X\amalg_VV prime. Thus cobase change sends the weak equivalence q_U to q, which has a nontrivial third homology obstruction.
references: Commentary: Carrying the local obstruction to the boundary

statement: An open--closed decomposition is a full sieve $A=X_0\hookrightarrow X$ and its complementary full cosieve $B=X_1\hookrightarrow X$; equivalently a functor $X\to[1]$ with fibres $A,B$.
notes: The source's open/closed terminology is directional: no arrow goes from B to A.

statement: $E=\widetilde X_{01}$ is the full subcategory of $\mathrm{Fun}([1],X)$ on arrows $f:a\to b$ with $a\in A,b\in B$; its morphisms $(u,v)$ satisfy $vf=f'u$.
notes: Ordinary arrow category with both sides of its squares forward; it is not the twisted-arrow category.

statement: The source projection $p:E\to A$ is a Grothendieck fibration with fibre $a\backslash B$ over $a$.
repair: Complete verification in 'The arrows which join the two pieces': precomposition gives a chosen cartesian lift $(u,\mathrm{id})$.

statement: The target projection $q:E\to B$ is a Grothendieck opfibration with fibre $A/b$ over $b$.
repair: Postcomposition gives chosen opcartesian lifts $(\mathrm{id},v)$; fibre morphisms are commuting triangles.

statement: The crossing arrows define a natural transformation $ip\Rightarrow jq$ and hence a homotopy-commutative square with vertices $E,A,B,X$; is it $W$-cocartesian?
repair: Affirmative for $W=\mathbf W_\infty$: the companion's directed-gluing proof constructs the canonical weak equivalence from its span homotopy colimit to $BX$.
notes: Open records the source's question, not the present status. The natural transformation, not an unspecified commutative square, fixes the comparison.

statement: If $i:A\to X$ is $W$-aspherical, the open--closed square is $W$-cocartesian.
repair: For $W_\infty$, each fibre $A/b$ of the opfibration $q$ is contractible, so $q$ and $i$ are weak equivalences; the span homotopy pushout is then equivalent to $X$.
notes: For a general W this uses the source's localizer and homotopy-colimit axioms.

statement: If $j:B\to X$ is $W$-coaspherical, the open--closed square is $W$-cocartesian.
repair: Dual argument: all fibres $a\backslash B$ of $p$ are W-aspherical, and $p$ and $j$ are weak equivalences under the stipulated axioms.

statement: For the structural functor $X\to[1]$, $W$-smoothness is equivalent to asphericity of $i$, and $W$-properness is equivalent to coasphericity of $j$.
repair: For the two-object base the nontrivial smoothness test is $A/b$ and the nontrivial properness test is $a\backslash B$; all tests at identity arrows have an extremal object.
notes: The words smooth and proper retain Grothendieck's localizer-dependent usage.

statement: The aspherical/coaspherical hypotheses imply respectively $i\in W$ or $j\in W$.
repair: This is the localizer form of the comma-category criterion.

statement: If $X$ is W-aspherical and $i\in W$ (respectively $j\in W$), then $A$ (respectively $B$) is W-aspherical.
repair: Two-out-of-three applied to the functors to the terminal category.

statement: Under $i\in W$ or $j\in W$ and W-asphericity of $X$, is the same square still W-cocartesian, in particular for $W=\mathbf W_\infty$?
repair: Yes for W∞ by the general directed-gluing formula; the extra hypotheses are unnecessary for that formula.
references: Cegarra2020, §3.1 and Theorem 3; commentary 'The open--closed gluing formula'
notes: This records the W∞ question separately from the false reflection inference in G12 and the ambiguously numbered axiom assumed in G13.

statement: For $W=\mathbf W_\infty$, under $i\in W$ (respectively $j\in W$) and W-asphericity of $X$, W-cocartesianness is equivalent to $q\in W$ (respectively $p\in W$).
gap_or_error: The opposite-side reflection inference is false in the stated $\mathbf W_\infty$ specialization. The ambiguously numbered Loc (6) in footnote 9 cannot be silently identified with a stronger axiom.
repair: The finite-poset example has $BA,BB,BX$ contractible and $BE$ acyclic but not simply connected; $i,j\in\mathbf W_\infty$ while $p,q\notin\mathbf W_\infty$, although the square is homotopy cocartesian. Reflection is valid conditional on the stronger reversible axiom of Chapter XVI, Corollary 3.7 (Loc (6C)); that axiom fails for $\mathbf W_\infty$.
references: Hatcher2002, Example 2.38 and Corollary 4.33; GrothendieckDerivateursXVI, §3, Corollary 3.7, ms26; commentary finite-poset development
notes: The conditional assertion under an explicit reversible axiom is not classified as false. What fails here is the W∞ reflection inference; the identity of the appendix's footnote-9 label with Chapter XVI's later convention is not certified.

statement: Footnote 9 explicitly assumes that W satisfies the previously introduced axiom Loc (6).
gap_or_error: The label is not expanded here and changes meaning across chapters: XV uses Loc (6) for fibrations, whereas XVI uses it for the full Mayer–Vietoris condition. The appendix's later Loc (6 a′) also differs typographically from XVI's Loc (6′ a).
repair: Retain the exact source hypothesis. Under the full reversible reading in XVI, §3, the conditional reflection is justified, but $\mathbf W_\infty$ does not satisfy that axiom: the proof maps the open-cover square of $X^{\mathrm{op}}$ to the terminal square and violates Loc (6b). No unique identification of the appendix label is asserted.
references: Grothendieck1990XV, §9, ms117; Grothendieck1990XIIa, §IV, ms53; GrothendieckDerivateursXVI, §3, ms16′–17′, footnote 13, and Corollary 3.7, ms26
notes: This is an explicit source assumption, not an axiom newly proved in the appendix. Distinguish an unresolved label identification from the proved failure of the precise XVI inverse condition for W∞.

statement: If $A\simeq e$ and $X,B$ are W-aspherical, must the attaching comma category $a\backslash B$ be W-aspherical, equivalently must $j$ be W-coaspherical?
gap_or_error: The PDF prints $e\backslash X$; the intended test is $e\backslash X_1$. The intended implication is false for W∞.
repair: Use the finite acyclic-link example: $A=\{a\}$, $B=\{b\}\cup K$, and $X=\{a,b\}\cup K$, with both new elements below K. Then $a\backslash B=K$ is not contractible although A,B,X are.
references: commentary 'Acyclic links and a false converse'
notes: Taken literally, $a\backslash X$ always has initial object $\mathrm{id}_a$. The source presents this as an unproved subsidiary case; the answer for W∞ is negative. This does not contradict the stronger conditional reflection axiom discussed in G13.

statement: $\mathcal X$ is the Grothendieck integral of the span $A\leftarrow E\to B$, with its canonical comparison $\varphi:\mathcal X\to X$ supplied by $ip\Rightarrow jq$.
repair: An explicit covariant span-Grothendieck model and its comparison are given in the directed-gluing proof.

statement: For every such decomposition, $\varphi\in\mathbf W_1$: it induces an equivalence of fundamental groupoids.
repair: Complete transport/gluing proof appears in 'From covering descent to higher local systems'; the stronger W∞ assertion is also proved.
notes: The source reports a proof and explains its covering-descent mechanism on ms18 but omits the full construction.

statement: The proposed path replacement $E'=\widetilde X'_{01}$ has objects $(a,b,c)$ with $a\in A,b\in B$ and $c$ a path from $a$ to $b$ in $X$.
gap_or_error: Morphisms and the precise path model are not specified in this excerpt.
repair: The commentary states explicitly when it uses a path category modeling the homotopy pullback BA×^h_BX BB; no claim about an unspecified raw path category is made.

statement: Replacing E by all paths can make the resulting comparison fail to belong even to $\mathbf W_1$.
repair: For $X=(a\rightrightarrows b)$ the arrow bridge has two objects, while the correct path bridge has homotopy type $\Omega S^1\simeq\mathbb Z$. Its span homotopy pushout has free fundamental group of countable rank and maps noninjectively to $\mathbb Z$.
notes: This confirms the assertion for a homotopically correct all-paths model.

statement: If $i$ or $j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, the all-paths replacement yields a weak equivalence to X.
repair: For a bridge modeling the homotopy pullback, one projection is then a weak equivalence; its span homotopy pushout is equivalent to the other endpoint and hence to X.
notes: A sufficient exception. The phrase 'sauf si' is not audited as a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of all exceptions.

statement: The author regards the open--closed phenomenon as peculiar to Cat, with no apparent analogue for spaces or simplicial sets.
repair: Read as a historical observation. The mixed-simplex proof supplies an explicit topological double mapping cylinder; Joyal's simplicial cylinders provide a directed simplicial analogue. An arbitrary complementary pair of topological subsets does not by itself supply a directed attaching category.
notes: This is not a theorem asserting nonexistence of every topological analogue.

statement: Pullback along $\varphi$ gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Rev}(X)\simeq\operatorname{Rev}(\mathcal X)$.
repair: Use transport functors to sets and the two mixed composition laws $\alpha_{fu}=\alpha_fL_A(u)$ and $\alpha_{vf}=L_B(v)\alpha_f$; they reconstruct the local system uniquely up to the displayed descent isomorphism.
notes: Completed in the commentary; all morphisms of local systems are included, not only object classification.

statement: $\operatorname{Rev}(\mathcal X)\simeq\operatorname{Rev}(A)\times^2_{\operatorname{Rev}(E)}\operatorname{Rev}(B)$.
repair: The categorical mapping cylinder inserts the isomorphism of pulled-back transport functors. Reconstruction of objects and morphisms gives the 2-pullback equivalence.

statement: The covering-descent argument should extend to higher homotopy degrees through n-gerbes.
repair: The needed higher-coefficient statement follows today from the proved homotopy pushout: $\operatorname{Fun}(BX,\mathcal S)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(BA,\mathcal S)\times^h_{\operatorname{Fun}(BE,\mathcal S)}\operatorname{Fun}(BB,\mathcal S)$, and similarly for n-truncated values.
notes: This supplies the relevant locally constant higher coefficients; it does not identify arbitrary gerbes/stacks with local systems.

statement: The author reports that the foundations of higher gerbes needed for this proof are unavailable to him, while Giraud supplies the degree-two background.
repair: Historical attribution retained; Giraud's book develops torsors, stacks and gerbes in nonabelian degrees one and two.
notes: Bibliography verification is publisher metadata/description only; no precise Giraud theorem is invoked.

statement: A verification sketched by the author in degree two gives $\varphi\in\mathbf W_2$.
gap_or_error: Footnote 10 reports the sketch but does not reproduce it.
repair: The full directed-gluing proof establishes W∞, hence the asserted W2 conclusion, without reconstructing an unavailable gerbe argument.

statement: For every open--closed decomposition, $\varphi\in\mathbf W_\infty$.
repair: Proved in the companion by the mixed-simplex/Thomason comparison, including compatibility with the canonical map.
notes: The conjecture is not left open in the delivered companion. The exact formulation was not found in the sources checked, so the specialization is marked ours without priority claim.

statement: If $W\supseteq\mathbf W_\infty$ satisfies Loc $(6\mathrm a')$, then the open--closed square is W-cocartesian.
gap_or_error: The exact numbered assumption is not uniquely identified: the appendix prints Loc (6 a′), while XVI's forward Mayer–Vietoris variant is Loc (6′ a), and XV uses the former pattern for a fibration variant.
repair: The canonical comparison belongs to $\mathbf W_\infty$ and hence to every $W\supseteq\mathbf W_\infty$. If the span Grothendieck construction represents the W-homotopy pushout, this yields W-cocartesianness. This sufficient comparison condition needs no opposite-side reflection. Chapter XVI, §3, ms24, footnote 15 explicitly supplies that span interpretation for fundamental localizers under its forward Loc (6′ a).
references: Grothendieck1990XV, §9, ms117; Grothendieck1990XIIa, §IV, ms53; GrothendieckDerivateursXVI, §3, ms17′ and ms24, footnote 15; commentary directed-gluing proof
notes: The W∞ theorem is fully established. The stronger full-XVI Loc (6) fails for W∞; the distinct literal label Loc (6 a′) is preserved without an unsupported historical identification.
